steps.title: One update per frame
steps.anchor: playdate.update = SceneManager.update
steps.html:
Playdate calls playdate.update() every frame.

What happens each frame depends on where we are: the title screen, the first-person maze, Tumble, or Slime. We call each of these a scene. We created SceneManager to keep track of the current scene and call its update function.

This assignment registers SceneManager.update as Playdate’s update callback. Without parentheses, it assigns the function rather than calling it.

SceneManager is imported before registration. Switching scenes changes the current scene used by that function, so the same callback keeps dispatching to the active scene.

steps.title: Delegate pause to the scene manager
steps.anchor: playdate.gameWillPause = SceneManager.pause
steps.html:
Register SceneManager.pause as the Playdate pause callback. It saves the active scene before calling that scene’s optional pause hook. Audio shutdown belongs to the scenes that play it.

Sleep, lock, and termination callbacks below continue to use SceneManager.save.

steps.title: Start at the title screen
steps.anchor:
SceneManager.onSwitch = SystemMenu.refresh
SceneManager.switch(TitleScene)
steps.html:
The first line stores SystemMenu.refresh as the callback to run after each scene switch. Without parentheses, it passes the function rather than calling it.

The second line calls SceneManager.switch(TitleScene): select the title scene, call its enter() function, then refresh the system menu through that callback.

Next, where does TitleScene come from?

steps.title: Load the title-screen file
steps.anchor: import "scenes/TitleScene"
steps.html:
Earlier in source/main.lua, this import loads the title scene before the startup calls run.

Playdate’s import runs source/scenes/TitleScene.lua once. Later imports of the same file do nothing.

Lua lets a call omit parentheses around a single string argument: import "scenes/TitleScene" is equivalent to import("scenes/TitleScene").

Standard Lua uses require; import is supplied by Playdate. This game uses it to load files that define shared globals.

Next, in source/scenes/TitleScene.lua, we’ll see the assignment that creates TitleScene.

SDK reference: imports

steps.title: Create the shared scene table
steps.anchor: TitleScene = { selection = 1, sizeIndex = Sizes.DEFAULT, rows = {} }
steps.html:
This assignment creates the global TitleScene because there is no local. After the import runs, source/main.lua can pass this table to SceneManager.switch.

The assignment creates the name, not the filename. The table initially holds the selected row, maze-size index, and menu rows.

steps.title: Keep a private input reader
steps.anchor: local controls = PlayInput.new()
steps.html: Each scene owns a local PlayInput reader. Hardware polling stays in that shared module; the reader is private to this scene.

steps.title: Read once, interpret the menu
steps.anchor:
local input = controls:read()
    local rows = TitleScene.rows
    local move = crankSteps:turn(input.crankChange)
    if input:isPressed(playdate.kButtonUp) then move = -1 end
    if input:isPressed(playdate.kButtonDown) then move = 1 end
    -- A press of the D-pad is a fresh start for the crank
steps.html:
controls:read() captures one hardware snapshot for this frame. input.crankChange feeds CrankSteps, while input:isPressed checks button edges from the same snapshot.

The scene still interprets menu actions: D-pad presses override crank movement and reset partial turns. After navigation clamps the highlight to a valid row, the scene resolves that row for left, right, and confirmation actions. A simultaneous turn and A therefore confirms the newly highlighted entry.

steps.title: Exit, replace, enter
steps.anchor:
function SceneManager.switch(scene, ...)
    if currentScene and currentScene.exit then currentScene.exit() end
    currentScene = scene
    if scene.enter then scene.enter(...) end
    if SceneManager.onSwitch then SceneManager.onSwitch(scene) end
end
steps.html: Let the old scene clean up, replace currentScene, then initialize the new scene. The ... passes its arguments through.

steps.title: Call the current scene
steps.anchor: function SceneManager.update() currentScene.update() end
steps.html: Only one scene receives updates. In first-person play, this calls FirstPersonScene.update() in source/scenes/FirstPersonScene.lua.

steps.title: Save through the scene
steps.html:
If the current scene provides save(), call it. Before a scene is selected, or in a scene without a save hook, do nothing.

FirstPersonScene.save() decides whether to store a run through SaveGame; EditorScene.save() keeps editor persistence separate. SceneManager does not choose a disk format or persistence policy.

steps.title: Save, then pause the active scene
steps.anchor:
function SceneManager.pause()
    SceneManager.save()
    if currentScene and currentScene.pause then currentScene.pause() end
end
steps.html: Reuse the save dispatch first, then call the current scene’s optional pause() hook. No scene, or no hook, is safe. The current scene remains selected; SceneManager knows nothing about audio.

steps.title: Three first-person submodes
steps.anchor: SUBMODES = { EXPLORE = "explore", DAILY = "daily", SCREENSAVER = "screensaver", CUSTOM = "custom" },
steps.html: Explore, Daily, and Screensaver share this scene and its 3D maze rules. Daily fixes the maze seed and size; Screensaver starts on autopilot without the puzzle. Tumble and Slime use separate scenes.

steps.title: Create the input reader and action mapper
steps.anchor:
local controls = PlayInput.new()
local walkingActions = WalkingActions.new(controls)
steps.html: PlayInput reads hardware. WalkingActions.new(controls) connects a mapper to that reader. The mapper translates its snapshot into movement and item actions and owns the button history.

steps.title: Reset transient state on entry
steps.anchor:
walkingActions = WalkingActions.new(controls)
    dockTimer = DockTimer.new()
    headBob = Bob.new()
steps.html: Fresh and resumed runs get a new walking mapper, dock timer, and head bob. The mapper keeps the existing controls reader but forgets button history from the previous visit, including B released in another scene.

steps.title: Read, map, update
steps.anchor:
local input = controls:read()
    local dockAction = dockTimer:update(input.isCrankDocked, input.current ~= 0 or input.pressed ~= 0)
    FirstPersonScene.applyDockAction(dockAction)
    local takingOver = game:isAutopilotOn() and input.pressed ~= 0
    if takingOver then game:setAutopilot(false) end
    game:update(walkingActions:read(takingOver, actionBuffer))
steps.html:
Read one hardware snapshot. dockTimer:update returns a handover action; FirstPersonScene.applyDockAction applies it to the scene’s game. Then map the snapshot into walking actions.

takingOver tells the mapper to consume item actions from the takeover press. The game receives only the resulting action table.

steps.title: Discard the run when restarting
steps.anchor:
function FirstPersonScene.restart()
    if FirstPersonScene.submode == FirstPersonScene.SUBMODES.CUSTOM and not FirstPersonScene.hasDesign() then
        SceneManager.switch(MyMazesScene)
        SaveGame.delete()
        return
    end
    if FirstPersonScene.submode ~= FirstPersonScene.SUBMODES.SCREENSAVER then SaveGame.delete() end
    FirstPersonScene.newGame(FirstPersonScene.game:isAutopilotOn())
end
steps.html:
A resumed custom run has no original drawing to restart. Switch to My mazes first so the outgoing exit hook finishes saving, then delete that save. The title will no longer offer Continue. Ordinary exits and pauses still save the run.

Other puzzle restarts delete the old save before generating the next maze; the screensaver leaves saves alone.

steps.title: Stop held audio for the system menu
steps.anchor:
function FirstPersonScene.pause()
    Sounds.stopHum()
    Music.stop()
end
steps.html:
Stop the shape hums and music so held notes cannot drone behind the system menu. Leaving the scene saves the run and reuses this pause hook. Tumble and Slime stop their music in their own pause and exit hooks; they do not play shape hums.

Returning from the system menu keeps the same run. The existing per-frame sound and music updates resume playback without a new restart callback.

steps.title: Draw the result
steps.anchor:
Sounds.play(game.events)
    Sounds.hum(game)
    -- The screensaver's music stays calm and level; otherwise it follows the way to the exit
    Music.update(game, FirstPersonScene.submode == FirstPersonScene.SUBMODES.SCREENSAVER and SCREENSAVER_MUSIC or nil)
    if game.hasEscaped then
        if FirstPersonScene.submode == FirstPersonScene.SUBMODES.SCREENSAVER then
            FirstPersonScene.restart()
        else
            SaveGame.delete()
            SceneManager.switch(EscapedScene, game.frames, FirstPersonScene.playAgain)
            return
        end
    end

    headBob:walk(FirstPersonScene.game.distanceWalked)
    MazeView.draw(FirstPersonScene.game, headBob:headOffset())
    Hud.draw(FirstPersonScene.game)
end
steps.html:
Play sounds, check for escape, then draw the world and HUD. Drawing the HUD last keeps it above the 3D image.

distanceWalked drives head bob from actual travel.

steps.title: Capture one frame
steps.anchor:
function PlayInput:read()
    self.current, self.pressed, self.released = playdate.getButtonState()
    self.crankChange = playdate.getCrankChange()
    self.crankPosition = playdate.getCrankPosition()
    self.isCrankDocked = playdate.isCrankDocked()
    return self
end
steps.html:
The three play modes use this reader. It records held, pressed, and released buttons, crank movement, crank angle, and whether the crank is docked.

These are hardware readings; their meaning depends on the game mode.

steps.title: Test a button bit
steps.anchor: function PlayInput:isDown(button) return self.current & button ~= 0 end
steps.html: Each button has its own bit in the mask. & keeps the bits shared by the mask and the requested button. A nonzero result means that button is down.

steps.title: Combine opposite directions
steps.html: Subtract the negative button from the positive button. Left alone gives −1, right alone gives +1, and both or neither gives 0.

steps.title: Own the button history
steps.html: The constructor stores the supplied controls reader. Each mapper owns its TapOrReel tracker. Reads return fresh actions unless the scene explicitly supplies its reusable output table. The tracker distinguishes tapping B from holding B while reeling.

steps.title: Map hardware to actions
steps.anchor:
actions.forward = input:axis(playdate.kButtonDown, playdate.kButtonUp)
    actions.turn = button:isHeld() and 0 or input.crankChange
    actions.crank = actions.turn
    actions.reel = reel
    actions.strafe = 0
    if input.isCrankDocked then
        actions.turn = sideways * DPAD_TURN_SPEED
    else
        actions.strafe = sideways
    end
    actions.pickUp = input:isPressed(playdate.kButtonA)
    actions.drop = isBTapped
steps.html:
Up/down moves forward/back. The crank turns the view unless B is held. Left/right turns when docked and strafes when undocked.

crank preserves actual crank movement for the gate; D-pad turning does not operate it.

steps.title: Consume the takeover press
steps.anchor:
if suppressItemActions then
        button:ignoreThisPress()
        actions.pickUp, actions.drop, actions.reel = false, false, 0
    end
steps.html: Suppress pickup, drop, and reel for this frame. Tell the B tracker to ignore the rest of this press too, so releasing it later cannot drop an item.

steps.title: Map the same controls for Tumble
steps.anchor:
actions.turn = input.crankChange
    actions.move = input:axis(playdate.kButtonLeft, playdate.kButtonRight)
    actions.jump = input:isPressed(playdate.kButtonA)
steps.html: Crank movement rotates the maze. Left/right moves the player. A, B, or up starts a jump on a fresh press.

steps.title: Map the same controls for Slime
steps.anchor:
actions.aim = input.crankPosition
    actions.isAimHeld = input:isDown(playdate.kButtonA)
    actions.cancel = input:isPressed(playdate.kButtonB)
    actions.move = input:axis(playdate.kButtonLeft, playdate.kButtonRight)
steps.html: Crank angle sets aim, holding A keeps aiming, and a fresh B press cancels. Left/right moves along a surface.

steps.title: Create the world
steps.anchor:
function Game.new(options)
    local maze = Maze.generate(options.columns, options.rows, options.random)
    local startX, startY = maze:cellCenter(1, 1)
    local startAngle = maze:hasPassage(1, 1, "east") and ANGLES.east or ANGLES.south
    local game = begin(maze, startX, startY, startAngle)
    if options.hasPuzzle then
        game.puzzle = Puzzle.scatter(maze, options.random)
    else
        maze:openExit()
steps.html:
Generate a maze, place the player in its first cell, and combine them in a Run. Face an open passage at the start.

A Lua table holds state; setmetatable lets it find the module’s methods.

steps.title: Choose one movement mode
steps.anchor:
if self.autopilot then
        self.autopilot:update()
        self.thread:record(self.player.x, fromY)
        self.thread:record(self.player.x, self.player.y)
    elseif reel > 0 then
        self:reelIn(reel)
        fromX, fromY = self.player.x, self.player.y
    else
        -- While the crank is lifting the gate it does not also swing the view
        if not isCrankingGate then self.player:turn(input.turn or 0) end
        self.player:move(self.maze, (input.forward or 0) * Game.WALK_SPEED, (input.strafe or 0) * Game.WALK_SPEED)
        self.thread:record(self.player.x, fromY)
        self.thread:record(self.player.x, self.player.y)
    end
    local walkedX, walkedY = self.player.x - fromX, self.player.y - fromY
steps.html:
Autopilot, thread reeling, and manual movement are exclusive branches. Manual movement scales input by Game.WALK_SPEED: 0.08 blocks per frame.

player:move(...) passes the player as self. The colon marks a method call.

steps.title: Measure what moved
steps.anchor:
local walkedX, walkedY = self.player.x - fromX, self.player.y - fromY
    self.distanceWalked = math.sqrt(walkedX * walkedX + walkedY * walkedY)
    self.blocksSinceStep = self.blocksSinceStep + self.distanceWalked
    if self.blocksSinceStep >= Game.STEP_BLOCKS then
        self.blocksSinceStep = self.blocksSinceStep - Game.STEP_BLOCKS
        self:emit("step")
    end
    local isPushing = not self.autopilot and reel == 0 and ((input.forward or 0) ~= 0 or (input.strafe or 0) ~= 0)
    if isPushing and self.distanceWalked == 0 and self.frames - self.lastBumpFrame >= Game.BUMP_FRAMES_APART then
        self.lastBumpFrame = self.frames
        self:emit("bump")
    end
steps.html: Subtract the old position and use √(dx² + dy²) for distance. Footsteps follow actual travel; a blocked push can produce a bump.

steps.title: Check interactions
steps.anchor:
self:visit()
    if self.flippers:touch(self.player.x, self.player.y) then
        self.isFlipped = not self.isFlipped
        self:emit("flip")
        self:say("The world turns over!")
    end
    if self.puzzle and input.pickUp then self:pickUp() end
    if self.puzzle and input.drop then self:drop() end

    self.hasEscaped = self.maze:isExit(self.player.x, self.player.y)
    if self.hasEscaped then self:emit("escape") end
steps.html:
Record the visited cell, handle flippers and shapes, then check whether the player entered the exit block.

The drawing code reads this state after the update.

steps.title: Ask the editor whether the drawing can play
steps.anchor:
function EditorScene.play()
    local design = EditorScene.editor:designToPlay()
    if not design then return end
    SceneManager.switch(FirstPersonScene, FirstPersonScene.SUBMODES.CUSTOM, TitleScene.sizeIndex, nil, design)
end
steps.html: designToPlay() returns a playable drawing or records the reason play is blocked. The scene handles navigation without writing the editor’s message or save state.

steps.title: Request a complete editing transition
steps.anchor: function EditorScene.randomMaze() EditorScene.editor:generateMaze(math.random) end
steps.html: The scene requests a new maze. MapEditor owns replacing the drawing, resetting the cursor and tool, and recording the change.

steps.title: Replace the drawing and reset the tools
steps.anchor:
function MapEditor:generateMaze(random)
    self.design = MapDesign.fromMaze(Maze.generate(self.design.columns, self.design.rows, random))
    resetCursor(self)
    self.message = "A new maze to alter"
    self.hasUnsavedChanges = true
end
steps.html: Generate a maze at the current size and convert it to a drawing. Use the same cursor initialization as a newly opened drawing: select the cells tool and snap to the cell nearest the entrance without moving the design’s start. Record the message and unsaved change in the same operation.

steps.title: Explain a blocked play attempt
steps.anchor:
function MapEditor:designToPlay()
    local problem = self.design:problems()[1]
    if problem then
        self.message = problem
        return nil
    end
    return self.design
end
steps.html: Validation can update the action message without marking the drawing dirty. A valid drawing is returned for play; only saving clears the dirty flag.

steps.title: Build a playable grid inside its owner
steps.anchor:
function Maze.fromDesign(design)
    assert(design.exit, "a playable maze needs an exit")
    local maze = Maze.new(design.columns, design.rows)
    for gridY = 1, maze.gridHeight do
        for gridX = 1, maze.gridWidth do
            maze.blocks[gridY][gridX] = design:isOpen(gridX, gridY) and Maze.BLOCKS.OPEN or Maze.BLOCKS.WALL
        end
    end
    maze.exitGridX, maze.exitGridY = design.exit.gridX, design.exit.gridY
    maze.blocks[maze.exitGridY][maze.exitGridX] = Maze.BLOCKS.DOOR
    return maze
end
steps.html: Maze copies the design’s open blocks and installs a closed exit gate. Game no longer constructs the grid through nested field writes. The copy lets play open the gate without changing the editor drawing.

steps.title: World positions to grid indices
steps.anchor:
function Maze:blockAt(x, y) return math.floor(x) + 1, math.floor(y) + 1 end -- luacheck: ignore 212/self

-- A wall or passage belongs with the cell before it up to its middle, and the next cell after
steps.html:
World x grows right; y grows down. Positions can be fractional. Grid indices start at 1.

(1.5, 1.5) becomes block (2, 2): floor each coordinate, then add one.

steps.title: Rooms separated by walls
steps.anchor:
local pitch = corridorWidth + 1
    for gridY = 1, maze.gridHeight do
        local line = {}
        for gridX = 1, maze.gridWidth do
            -- Wall lines run along every grid index that is one more than a multiple of the pitch
            local isCell = gridX % pitch ~= 1 and gridY % pitch ~= 1
            line[gridX] = isCell and Maze.BLOCKS.OPEN or Maze.BLOCKS.WALL
        end
        maze.blocks[gridY] = line
    end
steps.html:
pitch is corridor width plus one wall block. The remainder operator % places wall rows and columns.

With width 1, a 3 × 2-cell maze occupies 7 × 5 blocks. Tumble uses two-block corridors for jumping; Slime uses three-block corridors for throwing.

steps.title: Find unvisited neighbors
steps.anchor:
local visited = { [1] = true }
    local stack = { { 1, 1 } }
    while #stack > 0 do
        local column, row = stack[#stack][1], stack[#stack][2]
        local unvisited = {}
        for _, direction in ipairs(Maze.DIRECTIONS) do
            local nextColumn = column + Maze.OFFSETS[direction][1]
            local nextRow = row + Maze.OFFSETS[direction][2]
            local isInside = nextColumn >= 1 and nextColumn <= columns and nextRow >= 1 and nextRow <= rows
            if isInside and not visited[(nextRow - 1) * columns + nextColumn] then
                unvisited[#unvisited + 1] = direction
            end
        end
steps.html:
Start at cell (1, 1). The last entry of stack is the current cell; #stack is the list length.

The loop gathers neighboring cells that are inside the maze and have not been visited.

steps.title: Carve or backtrack
steps.anchor:
if #unvisited == 0 then
            stack[#stack] = nil
        else
            local direction = unvisited[random(#unvisited)]
            maze:carve(column, row, direction)
            local nextColumn = column + Maze.OFFSETS[direction][1]
            local nextRow = row + Maze.OFFSETS[direction][2]
            visited[(nextRow - 1) * columns + nextColumn] = true
            stack[#stack + 1] = { nextColumn, nextRow }
        end
steps.html:
Choose a random unvisited neighbor, carve the wall, and push that cell. If none remain, remove the stack’s last entry by assigning nil.

This is depth-first search. Connecting only new cells prevents loops: N cells get N − 1 internal passages.

experiments.title: Watch the stack work
experiments.html: Step through carving and backtracking. Cyan marks the current stack; gold marks its last cell.

steps.title: Follow a navigation target
steps.anchor:
function Player:walkTowards(targetX, targetY, speed)
    local offsetX, offsetY = targetX - self.x, targetY - self.y
    local distance = math.sqrt(offsetX * offsetX + offsetY * offsetY)
    if distance == 0 then return false end
    if distance <= speed then
        self.x, self.y = targetX, targetY
    else
        self.x = self.x + offsetX / distance * speed
        self.y = self.y + offsetY / distance * speed
    end
    return true
end
steps.html: Player owns the speed-limited move and exact arrival at a clear cell center. Autopilot chooses the route and asks for a step; it does not assign coordinates.

steps.title: Rewind position and heading together
steps.anchor:
function Player:rewindAlong(thread, distance, turnSpeed)
    local x, y, heading, blocked = thread:rewindFrom(self.x, self.y, distance)
    if not x then return false, blocked end
    ---@cast y number
    ---@cast heading number
    self.x, self.y = x, y
    local turn = (heading - self.angle + 180) % 360 - 180
    self:turn(math.max(-turnSpeed, math.min(turnSpeed, turn)))
    return true, blocked
end
steps.html: The thread checks its swept path. Player applies the resulting position and turns toward the backward heading at the allowed speed. If no clear movement remains, position and heading stay unchanged.

steps.title: Check the body’s four corners
steps.anchor:
local function isBlocked(maze, x, y)
    return maze:isWall(maze:blockAt(x - Player.RADIUS, y - Player.RADIUS))
        or maze:isWall(maze:blockAt(x + Player.RADIUS, y - Player.RADIUS))
        or maze:isWall(maze:blockAt(x - Player.RADIUS, y + Player.RADIUS))
        or maze:isWall(maze:blockAt(x + Player.RADIUS, y + Player.RADIUS))
end
steps.html: The player is a square, 0.4 blocks wide. Test all four corners at the proposed position. Walls and closed doors block movement.

steps.title: Stop at the wall edge
steps.anchor:
local function slide(from, to, isBlockedAt)
    if not isBlockedAt(to) then return to end
    local edge
    if to > from then
        edge = math.floor(to + Player.RADIUS) - Player.RADIUS - GAP
    else
        edge = math.ceil(to - Player.RADIUS) + Player.RADIUS + GAP
    end
    -- Only rest somewhere between where the body was and where it wanted to go
    local isBetween = (edge - from) * (to - from) >= 0
    if isBetween and not isBlockedAt(edge) then return edge end
    return from
end
steps.html:
Try the target first. If blocked, calculate a position just short of the wall. GAP avoids rounding a touching body into it.

This checks destinations, not the entire path. The game must use small movement steps.

steps.title: Slide along walls
steps.anchor:
function Player:moveBy(maze, offsetX, offsetY)
    local targetX, targetY = self.x + offsetX, self.y + offsetY
    self.x = slide(self.x, targetX, function(x) return isBlocked(maze, x, self.y) end)
    local isBlockedX = self.x ~= targetX
    self.y = slide(self.y, targetY, function(y) return isBlocked(maze, self.x, y) end)
    return isBlockedX, self.y ~= targetY
end
steps.html: Move x first, then y using the updated x. A wall can block one axis while allowing movement along the other.

steps.title: Rotate forward and sideways motion
steps.anchor:
function Player:move(maze, forward, strafe)
    local radians = math.rad(self.angle)
    local cosine, sine = math.cos(radians), math.sin(radians)
    self:moveBy(maze, cosine * forward - sine * strafe, sine * forward + cosine * strafe)
end
steps.html:
cos(angle) gives the horizontal part of forward; sin(angle) gives its vertical part. Lua takes radians, so convert degrees first.

Forward = (cos θ, sin θ). Right = (−sin θ, cos θ). At 90°, forward is down and right is left on the map.

experiments.title: Direction and angle
experiments.html: Change the heading. Compare the forward vector with its horizontal and vertical components.

steps.title: Start a queue at the exit
steps.anchor:
local queue, head = { { exitColumn, exitRow } }, 1
    while head <= #queue do
        local column, row = queue[head][1], queue[head][2]
        head = head + 1
        local distance = distances.byCell[(row - 1) * maze.columns + column]
        for _, direction in ipairs(Maze.DIRECTIONS) do
steps.html:
The exit cell has distance zero. Process the oldest queued cell first by advancing head.

This is breadth-first search: visit distance 0, then 1, then 2, and so on.

steps.title: Visit each reachable neighbor once
steps.anchor:
if isInside and not distances.byCell[key] and maze:hasPassage(column, row, direction) then
                distances.byCell[key] = distance + 1
                distances.farthest = math.max(distances.farthest, distance + 1)
                queue[#queue + 1] = { nextColumn, nextRow }
            end
steps.html:
Follow passages, assign the neighbor’s distance, and enqueue it. Every passage costs one step, so the first assigned distance is shortest.

Zero is true in Lua. The exit’s zero distance therefore still marks it as visited.

steps.title: Follow custom maps block by block
steps.anchor:
local function blockDistances(maze)
    local distances = setmetatable({ maze = maze, byBlock = {}, farthest = 0 }, ExitDistance)
    distances.byBlock[(maze.exitGridY - 1) * maze.gridWidth + maze.exitGridX] = 0
    local queue, head = { { maze.exitGridX, maze.exitGridY } }, 1
    while head <= #queue do
steps.html: Hand-made maps can connect between cell centers. Their breadth-first search starts at the gate, even while closed, and follows every open block. Walls and disconnected blocks have zero proximity.

steps.title: Convert distance to proximity
steps.html: Generated mazes measure cells; custom maps measure blocks, with proximity 1 at the gate. Proximity is 0 at the farthest reachable position. Music follows this corridor distance rather than straight-line distance through walls.

steps.title: Try left, ahead, right, back
steps.anchor:
local PREFERENCE <const> = { -1, 0, 1, 2 }

function Autopilot.chooseDirection(maze, column, row, facing)
    for _, quarterTurns in ipairs(PREFERENCE) do
        local direction = CLOCKWISE[(CLOCKWISE_INDEX[facing] - 1 + quarterTurns) % 4 + 1]
        if maze:hasPassage(column, row, direction) then return direction end
    end
    error("cell " .. column .. "," .. row .. " has no way out")
end
steps.html:
The numbers are quarter-turn offsets from the current heading. Choose the first open passage.

This works for the game’s tree-shaped maze, but does not choose the shortest route.

steps.title: Let Player perform the move
steps.anchor: if player:walkTowards(self.targetX, self.targetY, Autopilot.WALK_SPEED) then return end
steps.html: If a target step was needed, finish this frame. Once at the target, choose the next passage and turn before advancing.

steps.title: Turn by the shorter angle
steps.anchor:
local turn = (ANGLES[self.direction] - player.angle + 180) % 360 - 180

steps.title: Keep collision-safe path segments
steps.anchor:
function Thread:record(x, y)
    local points = self.points
    -- Nearer the point before last than the last point is: the player has turned back
    while #points >= 2 do
        local last, previous = points[#points], points[#points - 1]
        local isRetracing = distanceBetween(x, y, previous.x, previous.y)
            < distanceBetween(last.x, last.y, previous.x, previous.y)
        if not isRetracing or not Player.isPathClear(self.maze, previous.x, previous.y, x, y) then break end
        points[#points] = nil
    end
    local last = points[#points]
    if not Player.isPathClear(self.maze, last.x, last.y, x, y) then
        points[#points + 1] = { x = self.lastX, y = self.lastY }
        last = points[#points]
    end
    if distanceBetween(x, y, last.x, last.y) >= Thread.SPACING then points[#points + 1] = { x = x, y = y } end
    while #points > Thread.MOST_POINTS do
        table.remove(points, 1)
    end
    self.lastX, self.lastY = x, y
end
steps.html:
Record a point every 0.25 blocks, with extra points where a shortcut would cross a wall. Check clearance for the player’s whole body before removing a retraced point.

The scene’s game records both axes of movement. The list is capped at 800 points.

steps.title: Check the segment before rewinding
steps.anchor:
local share = stretch > 0 and math.min(1, distance / stretch) or 1
        local targetX, targetY = x + (last.x - x) * share, y + (last.y - y) * share
        if not Player.isPathClear(self.maze, x, y, targetX, targetY) then
            blocked = true
            break
        end
        if stretch > 0 then heading = math.deg(math.atan(y - last.y, x - last.x)) % 360 end
        x, y = targetX, targetY
steps.html:
share = distance / stretch, capped at 1, gives the fraction to rewind. Reeling 0.1 blocks along 0.25 blocks moves 40% of the segment.

Check the entire segment for body clearance before moving. Stop at blocked segments, including unsafe paths from older saves.

steps.title: Leave safe takeoff and landing space
steps.anchor:
function Spikes.place(maze, puzzle)
    local spikes = {}
    local startX, startY = maze:cellCenter(1, 1)
    local spawnGridX, landingGridY = maze:blockAt(startX, startY)
    -- Slime cannot steer or throw during this fall; its first landing must be safe.
    while not maze:isWall(spawnGridX, landingGridY + 1) do
        landingGridY = landingGridY + 1
    end
    for row = 1, maze.rows do
        for column = 1, maze.columns do
            local x = maze:cellCenter(column, row)
            local floorY = row * (maze.corridorWidth + 1)
            local gridX = math.floor(x) + 1
            local protected = (column == 1 and (row == 1 or floorY == landingGridY))
                or (column == maze.columns and row == maze.rows)
            for _, item in ipairs(puzzle.items) do
                local itemX, itemY = maze:blockCenter(item.gridX, item.gridY)
                local itemColumn, itemRow = maze:nearestCell(itemX, itemY)
                if itemColumn == column and itemRow == row then protected = true end
            end
            if not protected and maze:isWall(gridX, floorY + 1) and not maze:isWall(gridX, floorY) then
                spikes[#spikes + 1] = { x = x, y = floorY }
steps.html: Place short spike patches on solid floors, leaving the starting cell, its first landing below any open shaft, collectible cells, and exit cell clear. Slime cannot steer while falling, so the first landing remains safe on both entry and respawn. Each run owns its hazards. The triangles rotate with the maze in Tumble.

            and y + Player.RADIUS > spike.y - Spikes.HEIGHT
            and y - Player.RADIUS < spike.y

        end
    end

steps.title: Simulate one frame

local function fly(maze, body, velocityX, velocityY)
    velocityY = velocityY + Slime.GRAVITY
    local speed = math.sqrt(velocityX * velocityX + velocityY * velocityY)
    if speed > Slime.MAX_SPEED then
        velocityX, velocityY = velocityX * Slime.MAX_SPEED / speed, velocityY * Slime.MAX_SPEED / speed

    if isBlockedY and velocityY > 0 then
        surface = "floor"
    elseif isBlockedX then
        surface = velocityX > 0 and "right" or "left"
    elseif isBlockedY then
        surface = "ceiling"
    end
    return velocityX, velocityY, surface
end

For 70° FOV, tan(35°) ≈ 0.700. Tangent is opposite ÷ adjacent: plane half-width divided by one unit forward.

steps.title: Use a repeating threshold pattern
steps.html:
Playdate pixels are black or white. The Bayer matrix orders which pixels turn white to imitate gray.

At level 8, eight of the sixteen pixels are white. At level 16, all are white.

    local pattern = {}
    for row = 1, 8 do
        local byte = 0
        for column = 1, 8 do
            local isWhite = BAYER[(row - 1) % 4 + 1][(column - 1) % 4 + 1] < level

steps.title: Read shared sheet music

steps.html: The note book is immutable by contract. Sounds reads it without modifying it, and later calls never rewrite it. Each scheduled note reserves a synth until its release finishes, so long and overlapping effects keep every note. Finite effects continue on the sound clock across scene switches and paused game updates; stopping held hums does not cancel them. Copying these constants would add allocation without fixing an observed ownership violation.
